Do NOT use when you need the user's answer — this tool does not wait for a reply. Keep `answer` concise; for long material use a separate artifact and put only summary + path in `answer`. Omit `artifact_path` when there is no artifact; if the tool schema requires every key (strict mode), pass "" instead. When set, path must be non-empty.
turn_intermediate_reply.name: turn_intermediate_reply

answer.description: Concise intermediate user-facing text (status, partial insight, short clarification). Not a final task report. For long content: short summary here; full text in artifact.

artifact_path.description: Path to a detailed user-facing artifact when long content lives in a file.

turn_propose_plan.description: Finalizes turn: yes. Available ONLY in the 'plan' permission mode. Propose the finished implementation plan to the user for approval and end the turn. Call after research is complete; the user will approve, request rework, or cancel. Do NOT use for progress updates or questions (use turn_ask_human for questions). When a plan is already proposed and the user has not reviewed it yet, never replace it silently. A new request on the SAME task: propose an updated plan in full — the earlier steps plus the new ones, so nothing the user has not seen is lost. A request on SOMETHING ELSE: first ask via turn_ask_human whether to do the pending plan first, replace it, or merge both tasks into one plan, and propose only after they answer. When the user asks to SEE the current plan again or to approve it, do not retell it and do not claim it is approved: call this tool with show_current=true (and an empty plan) — the stored plan is shown again unchanged and the user gets the choice.
turn_propose_plan.name: turn_propose_plan

plan.description: The complete plan in markdown: goal, ordered steps, files to touch, verification. Self-contained — the user approves exactly this text.

show_current.description: true — show the plan already stored in the session again, unchanged (pass an empty plan). Use when the user asks to see or approve the current plan. Not for a plan under rework: propose the updated plan in full instead.

download_file.description: Downloads a document or plain-text file from an http(s) URL and saves it to the configured download directory under the project. Allowed extensions: csv, docx, html, json, md, msg, pdf, pptx, txt, xls, xlsx. Returns JSON with the absolute saved path for follow-up reading or analysis.
download_file.name: download_file

filename.description: Basename only, e.g. report.pdf. Must have an allowed extension.

exec_calculator.description: Evaluates an arithmetic expression (int/float) with operators + - * / // % ** and unary +/-, plus parentheses. This is NOT Python and not a sandbox: there are no function calls, no names, no attribute access, no subscripts, no containers (list/tuple/set/dict), no comprehensions, no booleans, no strings, no comparisons. Disallowed syntax is rejected before evaluation. Returns ok=true with value on success, ok=false with error on failure. Expression length is limited to max_expression_chars.
exec_calculator.name: exec_calculator

expression.description: Arithmetic expression, e.g. '1 + 2 * 3', '(1+2+3)*7', '2**10', '-3.5/2'. Only int/float literals and the operators + - * / // % ** with parentheses.

exec_command.description: Run a shell command synchronously. Returns JSON with ok, exit_code, stdout, stderr. The `timeout` argument is the deadline that kills the process; a `timeout` prefix inside the command does not extend it.
exec_command.name: exec_command

command.description: The command-line command to execute. Must be valid for the operating system and properly quoted, especially when paths contain spaces. Avoid interactive or destructive commands unless absolutely necessary.

cwd.description: Working directory for this command (absolute or relative). When unset, uses the current working directory.

env_vars.description: Optional environment variables to add/override for this command. Use [{name, value}] items. Values are converted to strings. If omitted, uses the current process environment.

run_in_background.description: Start the command detached and return without waiting for it to finish. Use for long-lived processes: dev servers, watchers, `npm run dev`, `uvicorn`. It keeps running after the agent exits. Stdout and stderr are not captured. A process still running is reported by pid. One that exits at once is an error with its exit code and no pid. Check a server by probing it (e.g. request its port). To see a startup error, run that command once in the foreground with a small `timeout`: the failure is in stdout/stderr, and a process that stays up is killed when the timeout elapses. That run does not leave it running — start the service again with this flag. Without this flag the command does not outlive the call. Appending `&` does not change that: on timeout or cancel the process group is killed, and the process dies with the agent. Output printed before that kill is in the reply.

timeout.description: Deadline for this call, in seconds. When it elapses the process is killed. Omit it and the default 200 applies (agent.exec_timeout_sec). A `timeout` prefix inside `command` does not extend this deadline. If the command needs longer, pass a larger number here.

exec_fetch_url.description: Fetches a URL via HTTP GET and returns extracted readable text when possible. Uses external network; does not execute local code or shell commands. If the response is binary (e.g., images, PDFs, archives), does NOT return raw bytes; instead returns content='binary data' with is_binary=true. Stores full extracted text in session in-memory cache by URL and supports paginated reads via offset/limit. Always returns a JSON string object: metadata fields first (ok, url, final_url, status_code, content_type, is_binary, result_type, extracted_source, truncated, error, pagination fields), then bulk text fields last (content, preview).
exec_fetch_url.name: exec_fetch_url

limit.description: Maximum number of characters to return in content. Default 20000.

max_preview_chars.description: Maximum number of characters for HTML/text preview in the response. Default 1200.

offset.description: Character offset for paginated reads from cached full content. Default 0.

proxy.description: Optional proxy URL for this request (http://, https://, socks5://, socks5h://, socks4://). Empty string or omit = no proxy.

timeout.description: HTTP timeout in seconds. Default is 20.

url.description: Absolute URL to fetch (http or https).

exec_python.description: Run Python code synchronously in a subprocess. Returns JSON with ok, return_code, stdout, stderr. The `timeout` argument is the deadline that kills the process.
exec_python.name: exec_python

code.description: The full Python code to execute via the current Python interpreter (fed on standard input; no temp script file).

cwd.description: Working directory for the subprocess (absolute or relative to the host). When unset, defaults to this agent's configured project/workspace root so relative paths resolve under the project. If the default is missing, read-only, or unsuitable, set cwd explicitly. When the tool returns an error with allowed_write_paths, use one of those paths as cwd (they are the permitted writable locations for this run).

env_vars.description: Optional environment variables to add/override as [{'name','value'}] pairs. Values must be strings.

timeout.description: Deadline for this call, in seconds. When it elapses the process is killed. Omit it and the default 200 applies (agent.exec_timeout_sec). If the code needs longer, pass a larger number here.

exec_sleep.description: Pauses execution for the given number of seconds before continuing. Maximum sleep duration is 180 seconds (3 minutes).
exec_sleep.name: exec_sleep

seconds.description: How long to sleep, in seconds (0 to 180).

fs_append_file.description: Append text to the end of an existing file (optional create). Checks encoding on a file head sample, then appends without loading the whole file into memory. Build large files with several moderate `content` chunks — not one huge append.
fs_append_file.name: fs_append_file

content.description: Text to append; keep each call a moderate size (e.g. one section or a few KB). For long output, chain many append-to-file calls instead of one huge payload.

create_if_missing.description: If true, creates the file if it does not exist. Default false.

encoding.description: Text encoding for the appended bytes: utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be (also windows-1251, iso-8859-1). Default utf-8. Must match the existing file head; if the head cannot be decoded as this encoding, append fails and the file is unchanged.

make_dirs.description: If true, creates parent directories when missing (used with create_if_missing). Default false.

path.description: The absolute path of the existing file to append to.

separator.description:
Text put between the current file end and the new content. Prefer two newlines unless another separator is needed; empty string means no separation. Use a real newline character (embedded in the JSON string as 
), not a literal backslash-n. Do not double-escape.

fs_apply_file_edits.description: Apply multiple literal search/replace edits to one file atomically. All edits are validated and applied in-memory first; if any edit fails, file is unchanged.
fs_apply_file_edits.name: fs_apply_file_edits

search.description: The exact content to find and replace. Use a unique multi-line snippet to avoid accidental matches elsewhere in the file.

encoding.description: Optional text encoding. Omit for UTF-8 (default; also UTF-16 with BOM). Otherwise: utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be (also windows-1251, iso-8859-1). Successful edits are written back in the same encoding.

expected_file_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest from file_info(include_hash=true). Batch aborts with stale_file if file content changed.

fs_file_info.description: Read-only file metadata for preflight before edits: type, size, mtime, permissions, readability, binary/text guess, optional line count, SHA-256.
fs_file_info.name: fs_file_info

fs_find_files_by_name.description: Find files and directories by name, path fragment, or glob under an absolute directory path. Searches the whole tree under path. Matches names and paths only — does not search file contents. query is a plain substring (file/dir name or path under path) or a glob (e.g. '*.py', '**/Config*.yml'). Short plain queries can match many paths. A query containing * ? [ or ] is read as a glob, so a name with literal brackets (e.g. 'report[1].pdf') cannot be matched exactly — search a bracket-free fragment of it instead. Does not enter nested directories named `.gc`, .git, __pycache__, node_modules, venv, or any nested directory whose name starts with '.'. If path itself is such a directory, it is still searched. case_insensitive defaults to true. At most max_matches results (default 100, maximum 300); truncated=true if the search stopped early.
fs_find_files_by_name.name: fs_find_files_by_name

case_insensitive.description: Ignore letter case when matching. Default true. Set false for case-sensitive match. Does not require an exact file name: query is still a substring or glob.

max_matches.description: Maximum matches to return. Default 100, maximum 300. truncated=true if more matches may exist.

path.description: Absolute directory to search under. Must be an existing directory.

query.description: Name or path fragment (e.g. 'list_files', 'tools/fs') or glob (e.g. '*.py', '**/*Config*.yml'). Plain text matches a substring of the file/dir name or of the path relative to path. Globs match the path relative to path; a glob without '/' matches at any depth. The mode is inferred: any of * ? [ ] makes the query a glob. So 'config[1].yml' is a character class and matches 'config1.yml', not the literal name — search 'config' instead.

fs_find_in_files.description: Search file contents under an absolute file or directory (not file names). Required: path, pattern. pattern is a Python regex by default (query_mode defaults to python-re). Optional query_mode: python-re (default), text (exact substring; metacharacters literal), python-re-dotall (cross-line '.'). At most limit matches (default 100, max 300); no pagination. Skips binary/large files; no .gitignore. Does not enter nested `.gc`, dirs named .git, __pycache__, node_modules, venv, or nested dot-dirs (path itself is still searched if it is one of those). Empty matches ≠ absent if the scan stopped early — check scan_complete / stop_* / guidance. search_backend=grep ran inside the sandbox; python read each candidate file from the host (fallback_reason says why). stop_reason=output_capped: grep output hit the transport ceiling — narrow pattern/path/file_pattern, not limit. prefilter=grep: candidate files were picked inside the sandbox by a fixed-string needle before any host read (ASCII case folding); prefilter=timeout|capped|failed: that pass gave up and every candidate was read from the host — narrow path/file_pattern.
fs_find_in_files.name: fs_find_in_files

case_insensitive.description: Ignore letter case when matching. Default false (case-sensitive, like grep). Set true for case-insensitive search.

exclude_dirs.description: Extra absolute directories to skip (each directory and everything under it). At most 32 entries.

file_pattern.description: When path is a directory: only search files whose path relative to path matches this glob. Basename-only patterns (no '/') match at any depth: '*.py' ≡ '**/*.py'. Patterns with '/' are path-globs ('src/*.ts' = one level under src/; 'src/**/*.ts' = recursive). Ignored when path is a single file.

limit.description: Maximum matches to return. Default 100, maximum 300.

path.description: Absolute file or directory path.

pattern.description: What to search for. Default query_mode=python-re: Python regular expression. query_mode=text: exact substring (metacharacters literal). query_mode=python-re-dotall: regex where '.' also matches newline.

query_mode.description: How to interpret pattern. Default python-re. python-re: Python regular expression ('.' does not match newline; ^/$ are line edges). text: exact substring only — metacharacters like | ( ) . * are literal; use when you need a fixed string that would be special in regex. python-re-dotall: same as python-re, but '.' also matches newline (only when a match must span lines).

show_excluded_dirs.description: Include the full list of directories skipped during the walk. Default false. Turn on only when you need to verify which dirs were not entered (hard excludes, dot-dirs, call exclude_dirs). Does not include search_stats.

fs_list_files.description: List files and directories under an absolute directory path. Default max_depth=0 lists only immediate children; raise max_depth to go deeper. Optional glob filters paths relative to path (only within max_depth). Does not search file contents. Shows normal folders as they are (including node_modules, .git, venv, etc.); omits the `.gc` directory. At most max_entries results (default 200); truncated=true if more exist.
fs_list_files.name: fs_list_files

glob.description: Optional filter on paths relative to path (e.g. '*.py', 'src/*'). Only entries within max_depth can match; use max_depth > 0 for nested globs.

max_depth.description: How deep to list. 0 = only immediate children of path (default). Higher values include nested directories.

max_entries.description: Maximum entries to return (files + directories). Default 200. truncated=true if the directory has more.

path.description: Absolute path of the directory to list. Must be an existing directory.

fs_read_file.description: Read a text file. Optional offset (1-based, default 1) and limit (default: to end of file) select a line window. Always includes full-file sha256 (for expected_file_sha256 in edit tools).
fs_read_file.name: fs_read_file

encoding.description: Omit for UTF-8 (UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM is detected). Otherwise one of: utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be.

limit.description: Max lines to read starting from offset. Default: to end of file.

offset.description: 1-based first line of the range to read. Default 1.

path.description: The path of the file to read. Must be a valid file path and not a directory.

fs_save_base64_file.description: Decodes a base64-encoded string and saves it as a binary file. Use this to persist images (screenshots, etc.) received as base64 data from MCP tools. To look at a saved image, call fs_view_image with its path. data must be standard base64 (A-Z a-z 0-9 + / =), ASCII only, with correct padding; no data URI prefix. Returns JSON with fields: ok, path, bytes_written, error.
fs_save_base64_file.name: fs_save_base64_file

data.description: Raw standard base64 content (A-Z a-z 0-9 + / =), ASCII only, with correct padding. Do not include a data URI prefix (e.g. data:image/png;base64,).

path.description: Absolute path where the file will be saved.

fs_search_and_replace.description: Replaces exact text in a file using literal matching. Uses literal string matching (case-sensitive, no regex). Supports dry-run, occurrence selection, optional backup, and optional unified diff output. When occurrence='all', expected_matches is required; if omitted, tool reports match_count and makes no changes. Always returns a JSON string with fields: ok, applied, matched, replaced, path, message, error.
fs_search_and_replace.name: fs_search_and_replace

backup.description: If true and file is modified, creates '<path>.bak' before writing.

diff_context_lines.description: Context lines for unified diff when return_diff=true. Default 3.

dry_run.description: If true, do not modify the file; only report whether replacement would happen.

encoding.description: Optional text encoding. Omit for UTF-8 (default; also UTF-16 with BOM). Otherwise: utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be (also windows-1251, iso-8859-1). Successful edits are written back in the same encoding.

expected_file_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest from file_info(include_hash=true). Edit aborts with stale_file if file content changed.

expected_matches.description: Required when occurrence='all' (if omitted, tool reports match_count and makes no changes). Otherwise optional: if provided, tool fails unless the total number of matches in the file equals this value.

max_diff_chars.description: Maximum number of characters returned in diff output. Default 12000.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence to replace: 'first' (default), 'last', 'all', or 1-based integer index. When 'all', you must also pass expected_matches equal to the total match count.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to modify. Must be a valid file path; directories are not allowed.

replace.description: The new content to replace the found content with. May be multiline. Can be empty to remove the matched content.

return_diff.description: If true, include a unified diff in the result.

search.description: The exact content to find and replace. Match is case-sensitive and literal (not regex). May be multiline. Cannot be empty. Use a unique multi-line snippet to avoid accidental matches elsewhere in the file.

fs_view_image.description: View an image file (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP, BMP, TIFF). Call it when a note in the history points to an image file, to inspect an image in the project, or to look at a screenshot an MCP tool returned: pass the path from the image block of that tool result ("type": "image", "path": ...), not a path mentioned in its text. An image attached to a message (not a note) is already in front of you — answer from it, do not call this tool for it. If you can see images, the image arrives in the next message; otherwise you get a text description of it. Use question to say what to look for.
fs_view_image.name: fs_view_image

path.description: Path of the image file.

question.description: What to look for in the image.

fs_write_file.description: Create or overwrite a text file (optional parent dirs). Keep each call small — stub or first section only. For long documents: minimal write here, then chain append calls with moderate chunks. Huge single `content` often breaks tool-call JSON. Prefer this when you need a new file or full replace; use append to grow an existing file. Pass encoding= to write non-UTF-8 (e.g. cp1251).
fs_write_file.name: fs_write_file

backup.description: If true and file exists, creates a backup copy at '<path>.bak' before writing. Default false.

content.description: Text to write; must be short. For large output: use a placeholder or opening section only, then add the bulk via several append-to-file calls. For code/config, keep to one small file or split across an initial write and appends.

encoding.description: Text encoding to write: utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be (also windows-1251, iso-8859-1). Default utf-8.

make_dirs.description: If true, creates any missing parent folders before writing. Set true when the target file's parent folder does not exist yet. Default false — the write fails with 'parent_not_found' if the parent folder is missing.

mode.description: Write mode: 'overwrite' (default), 'create_only' (fail if exists), or 'fail_if_missing' (fail if missing).

path.description: The absolute path of the file to write to. Must be an absolute path, not relative. Ensure the file location is valid and accessible.

project_memory.description: Project/long memory: durable facts for FUTURE sessions ('remember this rule', conventions, artifact-first preferences, stable decisions). Not for turn-by-turn chat progress — use thread memory. Survives restarts. Actions: read, append (short delta), write (full replace / full overwrite; rare). Reports fill percent. Append verified bullets only; no secrets, chain-of-thought, or guesses as facts.
project_memory.name: project_memory

action.description: read = return the current memory content; append = add ONLY the new delta at end; write = fully replace the memory (full overwrite; rare).

content.description: Markdown text for append/write. Required for every action; ignored for read. For append: ONLY the new delta. For write: the FULL updated markdown (full overwrite). For read: pass empty string "".

session_memory.description: Thread/session memory for THIS dialogue only — not project-wide 'remember forever'. Do not append on every trivial step; update after meaningful progress or before handoff/delegation. This tool does NOT write files to disk. Stores compact state that survives dialog summarization. Use fixed registers only: goal = user intent, desired outcome, success criteria, definition of done; constraints = hard requirements, preferences, prohibitions, format/technical/safety limits; state = blockers, active hypotheses, findings in progress, decisions still open — narrative working state. The step-by-step plan with statuses belongs in the session_todo checklist tool when it is available; if that tool is NOT available, keep the plan here instead. Never keep the same steps in both places; knowledge = stable verified facts, architecture decisions, implementation notes, artifact references, evidence. Actions: list, read, append (short delta), write (full replace of one register; rare). Every response includes per-register length vs limit in registers. Use append for compact new deltas only. Use write for full replace: compaction, cleanup, deduplication, or removing obsolete information. Maintenance: when register sizes in that metadata approach or exceed limits, proactively compact the affected register—read it, then write the compact full replacement (deduplicate, drop obsolete detail; do not keep appending into an overfull register). Move bulky details to a file/artifact when needed; keep a concise form of what belongs in that register per the definitions above (e.g. facts, decisions, blockers, artifact links—not chain-of-thought or raw dumps). Do not wait for the user to ask; memory hygiene is part of using this tool. Do NOT store chain-of-thought, verbose reasoning, raw logs, large blobs, full file contents, repetitive history, or transient chatter. Register selection: objective/done criteria -> goal; requirements/preferences -> constraints; blocker/hypothesis/open decision -> state; stable fact/decision/artifact/evidence -> knowledge; step-by-step plan and step statuses -> session_todo tool when available, otherwise -> state. If unsure: an actionable STEP of the task -> session_todo (or state if that tool is absent); other unresolved information -> state; stable reusable information -> knowledge; requirement/preference -> constraints; desired outcome -> goal. Keep memory compact, structured, and durable.
session_memory.name: session_memory

action.description: list = show register sizes; read = return one register; append = add ONLY the new delta; write = fully replace one register (rare; full overwrite).

content.description: Markdown text for append/write. For append: ONLY the new delta. For write: the FULL updated register content (full overwrite).

reason.description: Optional brief justification for why this update is useful and why it belongs in this register. Recommended but optional; content is required for append/write.

register.description: Target memory register. Required for every action (ignored for list).

session_read_stored_tool_output.description: Read a paginated fragment of a previously stored large tool output by output_ref. Pagination uses **characters** (Unicode code points): `offset` + `limit`. Response pages include truncated, total_chars, next_offset, returned_chars. EOF: when truncated=false, next_offset equals total_chars (end of body).
session_read_stored_tool_output.name: session_read_stored_tool_output

limit.description: Max characters to return from offset (not lines or records). Clamped to tool_output_inline_max_chars.

offset.description: Character offset (Unicode code points) into the stored body. Default: 0.

session_think.description: Think out loud during the current turn. Use it when complex reasoning, self-critique, or structured reflection is needed. Content is NOT saved to thread memory or any other durable storage—it only exists in the current dialogue context. If your think output contains a specific Decision / Canonical target / Plan completed / Verified fact, record it separately via the thread memory tool (append) when one is available so it can persist across summarization.
session_think.name: session_think

critics.description: Self-critique: what could be wrong, weak points, alternative views.

doubts.description: Uncertainties, open questions, or things that need verification.

reflection.description: Synthesis or meta-reflection: main takeaways, conclusions, next steps.

thoughts.description: Reasoning, hypotheses, or exploration of ideas.

session_todo.description: Task checklist for the CURRENT task — your plan and progress tracker. USE IT PROACTIVELY, without being asked: write the checklist BEFORE starting work whenever the task has 3+ logical steps, several deliverables, or a list of requirements to satisfy. Planning on paper first is how you avoid dropping requirements halfway through — do not rely on memory for multi-step work. Then keep it current as you go: mark a step completed right after finishing it and set the next one to in_progress (exactly one in_progress at a time); add steps when new work surfaces. Each call FULLY REPLACES the checklist with the list you pass; replace the whole list when the task itself changes, pass an empty list to clear it. Skip the checklist only for genuinely trivial or single-step tasks. It survives dialog summarization and is shown to the user as live progress.
session_todo.name: session_todo

todos.description: Full replacement checklist: every remaining and completed step of the current task, in execution order.

content.description: Step formulation (imperative, concise).

skills_list.description: List available local skills. By default returns flat skills plus one entry per pack (the pack's bootstrap skill, marked with 'is_pack_bootstrap': true and 'pack_size': N). Internal pack skills are hidden by default. Use the 'pack' parameter to drill into a specific pack's internal skills. Each list entry has fields: id (canonical, '<pack-id>:<skill-id>' for pack skills), name, description, source (system/user/project), pack_id (string for pack skills, null for flat), is_pack_bootstrap (bool). Bootstrap entries also have 'pack_size' (total internal skills count). Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, error, result}.
skills_list.name: skills_list

pack.description: Pack ID to drill into internal skills only (including bootstrap). When unset, returns flat skills plus one bootstrap entry per pack.

skills_load.description: Load a specific skill by its id — the FIRST step for any skill, before skills_read_reference or skills_read_asset. Returns metadata, instructions, and lists of available references and assets (load those by name afterwards if needed). Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, skill_id, error, result}. On success, result.skill contains the skill detail.
skills_load.name: skills_load

skill_id.description: The id of the skill to load.

skills_read_asset.description: Load ONE supplementary asset file of a skill by slug. This does NOT load the skill itself — call skills_load(skill_id) FIRST to get the skill's instructions and the exact asset names. Use only slug values listed by skills_load (or returned in this tool's error); never invent a slug. Assets live under the skill's assets/ directory. Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, skill_id, slug, error, result}. On success, the asset content is inside result.
skills_read_asset.name: skills_read_asset

skill_id.description: The id of the skill whose asset you want to load.

slug.description: Slug of the asset. Maps to a file path inside assets/, without extension, with '/' as path separator.

skills_read_reference.description: Load ONE supplementary reference file of a skill by slug. This does NOT load the skill itself — call skills_load(skill_id) FIRST to get the skill's instructions and the exact reference names. Use only slug values listed by skills_load (or returned in this tool's error); never invent a slug. References live under the skill's references/ directory. Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, skill_id, slug, error, result}. On success, the reference content is inside result.
skills_read_reference.name: skills_read_reference

skill_id.description: The id of the skill whose reference you want to load.

slug.description: Slug of the reference. Maps to a file path inside references/, without extension, with '/' as path separator.

skills_run_script.description: Run a Python script that belongs to a specific skill. script_name is required and must be one of the skill's listed scripts. Use argv for CLI positional arguments and flags (for example, '--input report.pdf'). args is a legacy JSON object string, supplied to stdin only when argv is absent. Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, script_ok, skill_id, script_name, argv, args, error, result}. ok=true means the wrapper launched the script; script_ok=false when result.exit_code != 0. On success, the script output is inside result.
skills_run_script.name: skills_run_script

args.description: Must decode to a JSON object (dictionary), not an array, scalar, or null. When provided, pass script arguments as one JSON string (this field is string-typed, not a nested object). The script receives the parsed object on stdin and must read it explicitly (keys are not converted to CLI flags or positionals). Example: '{"input":"hello","limit":3}'.

argv.description: CLI arguments passed after the script path, as entered in a terminal. Example: '--input report.pdf --format json'. When set, args is ignored.

script_name.description: Required script file name inside the skill's scripts/ directory. Use an exact name returned by skills_load; the scripts/ prefix is accepted.

skill_id.description: The id of the skill whose script should be executed.

turn_ask_human.description: Finalizes turn: no. Request user input and wait for their reply. Use to ask for a choice, clarification, missing data, or explicit confirmation before risky or irreversible actions. Do NOT use for one-way status or explanations. Do NOT use as the final report of a completed task or to end the current user turn. Be clear and include necessary context; avoid vague questions. The `question` must be concise: the actual question plus minimal context only. Do not put long comparisons or background dumps into `question`; put detailed material in a separate artifact and reference it briefly here. When a finite choice set fits, prefer explicit options (A/B/C, numbered list, yes/no). After each call, follow the hint field in the tool result to classify and act on the reply.
turn_ask_human.name: turn_ask_human

question.description: Concise question to the human (markdown ok): what you need from them, minimal context, and explicit options when choices are known. Not for long content — use an artifact + short pointer here.

turn_finish.description: Finalizes turn: yes. Call exactly once when you end the current user turn (not the whole thread/session). Use for done / partial / blocked outcomes with a self-contained report and machine-readable handoff. Do NOT use for brainstorming, mid-task status, or progress while work continues. Call only after reasonable work and verification for this turn when needed. Do not call early just to return control.
turn_finish.name: turn_finish

comment.description: Caveats, risks, unresolved items, or suggested next steps for the user.

handoff.description: Must decode to a JSON object (dictionary), not an array, scalar, or null. Pass the object as one JSON string (this field is string-typed, not a nested object). Machine-readable payload for downstream workflows; use "{}" when nothing extra is needed. Example: '{"artifacts":["report.md"]}'.

solution_type.description: Turn outcome: full_solution (objective done), partial_solution (meaningful progress, not done), direct_answer (direct answer/explanation completed this turn), couldnt_solve, need_additional_info (blocked), abandoned.

task.description: What the user asked this turn, in 1–2 phrases, in the user's terms. Not what was done — that is task_report.

task_report.description: Final human-facing summary for this turn: what was done, result, assumptions, evidence. Plain text, no markdown. Max 10000 characters. Not for mid-task status updates.

turn_intermediate_reply.description: Finalizes turn: no. Intermediate user-visible reply: status, hypothesis, mini-explanation, or progress update. The current task is NOT complete — you will continue with more tools after this. Do NOT use for the final report of a multi-step task or to end the current user turn. Do NOT use when you need the user's answer — this tool does not wait for a reply. Keep `answer` concise; for long material use a separate artifact and put only summary + path in `answer`. Omit `artifact_path` when there is no artifact; if the tool schema requires every key (strict mode), pass "" instead. When set, path must be non-empty.
turn_intermediate_reply.name: turn_intermediate_reply

answer.description: Concise intermediate user-facing text (status, partial insight, short clarification). Not a final task report. For long content: short summary here; full text in artifact.

artifact_path.description: Path to a detailed user-facing artifact when long content lives in a file.

turn_propose_plan.description: Finalizes turn: yes. Available ONLY in the 'plan' permission mode. Propose the finished implementation plan to the user for approval and end the turn. Call after research is complete; the user will approve, request rework, or cancel. Do NOT use for progress updates or questions (use turn_ask_human for questions). When a plan is already proposed and the user has not reviewed it yet, never replace it silently. A new request on the SAME task: propose an updated plan in full — the earlier steps plus the new ones, so nothing the user has not seen is lost. A request on SOMETHING ELSE: first ask via turn_ask_human whether to do the pending plan first, replace it, or merge both tasks into one plan, and propose only after they answer. When the user asks to SEE the current plan again or to approve it, do not retell it and do not claim it is approved: call this tool with show_current=true (and an empty plan) — the stored plan is shown again unchanged and the user gets the choice.
turn_propose_plan.name: turn_propose_plan

plan.description: The complete plan in markdown: goal, ordered steps, files to touch, verification. Self-contained — the user approves exactly this text.

show_current.description: true — show the plan already stored in the session again, unchanged (pass an empty plan). Use when the user asks to see or approve the current plan. Not for a plan under rework: propose the updated plan in full instead.

download_file.description: Downloads a document or plain-text file from an http(s) URL and saves it to the configured download directory under the project. Allowed extensions: csv, docx, html, json, md, msg, pdf, pptx, txt, xls, xlsx. Returns JSON with the absolute saved path for follow-up reading or analysis.
download_file.name: download_file

filename.description: Basename only, e.g. report.pdf. Must have an allowed extension.

exec_calculator.description: Evaluates an arithmetic expression (int/float) with operators + - * / // % ** and unary +/-, plus parentheses. This is NOT Python and not a sandbox: there are no function calls, no names, no attribute access, no subscripts, no containers (list/tuple/set/dict), no comprehensions, no booleans, no strings, no comparisons. Disallowed syntax is rejected before evaluation. Returns ok=true with value on success, ok=false with error on failure. Expression length is limited to max_expression_chars.
exec_calculator.name: exec_calculator

expression.description: Arithmetic expression, e.g. '1 + 2 * 3', '(1+2+3)*7', '2**10', '-3.5/2'. Only int/float literals and the operators + - * / // % ** with parentheses.

exec_command.description: Run a shell command synchronously. Returns JSON with ok, exit_code, stdout, stderr. The `timeout` argument is the deadline that kills the process; a `timeout` prefix inside the command does not extend it.
exec_command.name: exec_command

command.description: The command-line command to execute. Must be valid for the operating system and properly quoted, especially when paths contain spaces. Avoid interactive or destructive commands unless absolutely necessary.

cwd.description: Working directory for this command (absolute or relative). When unset, uses the current working directory.

env_vars.description: Optional environment variables to add/override for this command. Use [{name, value}] items. Values are converted to strings. If omitted, uses the current process environment.

run_in_background.description: Start the command detached and return without waiting for it to finish. Use for long-lived processes: dev servers, watchers, `npm run dev`, `uvicorn`. It keeps running after the agent exits. Stdout and stderr are not captured. A process still running is reported by pid. One that exits at once is an error with its exit code and no pid. Check a server by probing it (e.g. request its port). To see a startup error, run that command once in the foreground with a small `timeout`: the failure is in stdout/stderr, and a process that stays up is killed when the timeout elapses. That run does not leave it running — start the service again with this flag. Without this flag the command does not outlive the call. Appending `&` does not change that: on timeout or cancel the process group is killed, and the process dies with the agent. Output printed before that kill is in the reply.

timeout.description: Deadline for this call, in seconds. When it elapses the process is killed. Omit it and the default 200 applies (agent.exec_timeout_sec). A `timeout` prefix inside `command` does not extend this deadline. If the command needs longer, pass a larger number here.

exec_fetch_url.description: Fetches a URL via HTTP GET and returns extracted readable text when possible. Uses external network; does not execute local code or shell commands. If the response is binary (e.g., images, PDFs, archives), does NOT return raw bytes; instead returns content='binary data' with is_binary=true. Stores full extracted text in session in-memory cache by URL and supports paginated reads via offset/limit. Always returns a JSON string object: metadata fields first (ok, url, final_url, status_code, content_type, is_binary, result_type, extracted_source, truncated, error, pagination fields), then bulk text fields last (content, preview).
exec_fetch_url.name: exec_fetch_url

limit.description: Maximum number of characters to return in content. Default 20000.

max_preview_chars.description: Maximum number of characters for HTML/text preview in the response. Default 1200.

offset.description: Character offset for paginated reads from cached full content. Default 0.

proxy.description: Optional proxy URL for this request (http://, https://, socks5://, socks5h://, socks4://). Empty string or omit = no proxy.

timeout.description: HTTP timeout in seconds. Default is 20.

url.description: Absolute URL to fetch (http or https).

exec_python.description: Run Python code synchronously in a subprocess. Returns JSON with ok, return_code, stdout, stderr. The `timeout` argument is the deadline that kills the process.
exec_python.name: exec_python

code.description: The full Python code to execute via the current Python interpreter (fed on standard input; no temp script file).

cwd.description: Working directory for the subprocess (absolute or relative to the host). When unset, defaults to this agent's configured project/workspace root so relative paths resolve under the project. If the default is missing, read-only, or unsuitable, set cwd explicitly. When the tool returns an error with allowed_write_paths, use one of those paths as cwd (they are the permitted writable locations for this run).

env_vars.description: Optional environment variables to add/override as [{'name','value'}] pairs. Values must be strings.

timeout.description: Deadline for this call, in seconds. When it elapses the process is killed. Omit it and the default 200 applies (agent.exec_timeout_sec). If the code needs longer, pass a larger number here.

exec_sleep.description: Pauses execution for the given number of seconds before continuing. Maximum sleep duration is 180 seconds (3 minutes).
exec_sleep.name: exec_sleep

seconds.description: How long to sleep, in seconds (0 to 180).

fs_append_file.description: Append text to the end of an existing file (optional create). Checks encoding on a file head sample, then appends without loading the whole file into memory. Build large files with several moderate `content` chunks — not one huge append.
fs_append_file.name: fs_append_file

content.description: Text to append; keep each call a moderate size (e.g. one section or a few KB). For long output, chain many append-to-file calls instead of one huge payload.

create_if_missing.description: If true, creates the file if it does not exist. Default false.

encoding.description: Text encoding for the appended bytes: utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be (also windows-1251, iso-8859-1). Default utf-8. Must match the existing file head; if the head cannot be decoded as this encoding, append fails and the file is unchanged.

make_dirs.description: If true, creates parent directories when missing (used with create_if_missing). Default false.

path.description: The absolute path of the existing file to append to.

separator.description:
Text put between the current file end and the new content. Prefer two newlines unless another separator is needed; empty string means no separation. Use a real newline character (embedded in the JSON string as 
), not a literal backslash-n. Do not double-escape.

fs_apply_file_edits.description: Apply multiple literal search/replace edits to one file atomically. All edits are validated and applied in-memory first; if any edit fails, file is unchanged.
fs_apply_file_edits.name: fs_apply_file_edits

search.description: The exact content to find and replace. Use a unique multi-line snippet to avoid accidental matches elsewhere in the file.

encoding.description: Optional text encoding. Omit for UTF-8 (default; also UTF-16 with BOM). Otherwise: utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be (also windows-1251, iso-8859-1). Successful edits are written back in the same encoding.

expected_file_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest from file_info(include_hash=true). Batch aborts with stale_file if file content changed.

fs_file_info.description: Read-only file metadata for preflight before edits: type, size, mtime, permissions, readability, binary/text guess, optional line count, SHA-256.
fs_file_info.name: fs_file_info

fs_find_files_by_name.description: Find files and directories by name, path fragment, or glob under an absolute directory path. Searches the whole tree under path. Matches names and paths only — does not search file contents. query is a plain substring (file/dir name or path under path) or a glob (e.g. '*.py', '**/Config*.yml'). Short plain queries can match many paths. A query containing * ? [ or ] is read as a glob, so a name with literal brackets (e.g. 'report[1].pdf') cannot be matched exactly — search a bracket-free fragment of it instead. Does not enter nested directories named `.gc`, .git, __pycache__, node_modules, venv, or any nested directory whose name starts with '.'. If path itself is such a directory, it is still searched. case_insensitive defaults to true. At most max_matches results (default 100, maximum 300); truncated=true if the search stopped early.
fs_find_files_by_name.name: fs_find_files_by_name

case_insensitive.description: Ignore letter case when matching. Default true. Set false for case-sensitive match. Does not require an exact file name: query is still a substring or glob.

max_matches.description: Maximum matches to return. Default 100, maximum 300. truncated=true if more matches may exist.

path.description: Absolute directory to search under. Must be an existing directory.

query.description: Name or path fragment (e.g. 'list_files', 'tools/fs') or glob (e.g. '*.py', '**/*Config*.yml'). Plain text matches a substring of the file/dir name or of the path relative to path. Globs match the path relative to path; a glob without '/' matches at any depth. The mode is inferred: any of * ? [ ] makes the query a glob. So 'config[1].yml' is a character class and matches 'config1.yml', not the literal name — search 'config' instead.

fs_find_in_files.description: Search file contents under an absolute file or directory (not file names). Required: path, pattern. pattern is a Python regex by default (query_mode defaults to python-re). Optional query_mode: python-re (default), text (exact substring; metacharacters literal), python-re-dotall (cross-line '.'). At most limit matches (default 100, max 300); no pagination. Skips binary/large files; no .gitignore. Does not enter nested `.gc`, dirs named .git, __pycache__, node_modules, venv, or nested dot-dirs (path itself is still searched if it is one of those). Empty matches ≠ absent if the scan stopped early — check scan_complete / stop_* / guidance. search_backend=grep ran inside the sandbox; python read each candidate file from the host (fallback_reason says why). stop_reason=output_capped: grep output hit the transport ceiling — narrow pattern/path/file_pattern, not limit. prefilter=grep: candidate files were picked inside the sandbox by a fixed-string needle before any host read (ASCII case folding); prefilter=timeout|capped|failed: that pass gave up and every candidate was read from the host — narrow path/file_pattern.
fs_find_in_files.name: fs_find_in_files

case_insensitive.description: Ignore letter case when matching. Default false (case-sensitive, like grep). Set true for case-insensitive search.

exclude_dirs.description: Extra absolute directories to skip (each directory and everything under it). At most 32 entries.

file_pattern.description: When path is a directory: only search files whose path relative to path matches this glob. Basename-only patterns (no '/') match at any depth: '*.py' ≡ '**/*.py'. Patterns with '/' are path-globs ('src/*.ts' = one level under src/; 'src/**/*.ts' = recursive). Ignored when path is a single file.

limit.description: Maximum matches to return. Default 100, maximum 300.

path.description: Absolute file or directory path.

pattern.description: What to search for. Default query_mode=python-re: Python regular expression. query_mode=text: exact substring (metacharacters literal). query_mode=python-re-dotall: regex where '.' also matches newline.

query_mode.description: How to interpret pattern. Default python-re. python-re: Python regular expression ('.' does not match newline; ^/$ are line edges). text: exact substring only — metacharacters like | ( ) . * are literal; use when you need a fixed string that would be special in regex. python-re-dotall: same as python-re, but '.' also matches newline (only when a match must span lines).

show_excluded_dirs.description: Include the full list of directories skipped during the walk. Default false. Turn on only when you need to verify which dirs were not entered (hard excludes, dot-dirs, call exclude_dirs). Does not include search_stats.

fs_list_files.description: List files and directories under an absolute directory path. Default max_depth=0 lists only immediate children; raise max_depth to go deeper. Optional glob filters paths relative to path (only within max_depth). Does not search file contents. Shows normal folders as they are (including node_modules, .git, venv, etc.); omits the `.gc` directory. At most max_entries results (default 200); truncated=true if more exist.
fs_list_files.name: fs_list_files

glob.description: Optional filter on paths relative to path (e.g. '*.py', 'src/*'). Only entries within max_depth can match; use max_depth > 0 for nested globs.

max_depth.description: How deep to list. 0 = only immediate children of path (default). Higher values include nested directories.

max_entries.description: Maximum entries to return (files + directories). Default 200. truncated=true if the directory has more.

path.description: Absolute path of the directory to list. Must be an existing directory.

fs_read_file.description: Read a text file. Optional offset (1-based, default 1) and limit (default: to end of file) select a line window. Always includes full-file sha256 (for expected_file_sha256 in edit tools).
fs_read_file.name: fs_read_file

encoding.description: Omit for UTF-8 (UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM is detected). Otherwise one of: utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be.

limit.description: Max lines to read starting from offset. Default: to end of file.

offset.description: 1-based first line of the range to read. Default 1.

path.description: The path of the file to read. Must be a valid file path and not a directory.

fs_save_base64_file.description: Decodes a base64-encoded string and saves it as a binary file. Use this to persist images (screenshots, etc.) received as base64 data from MCP tools. To look at a saved image, call fs_view_image with its path. data must be standard base64 (A-Z a-z 0-9 + / =), ASCII only, with correct padding; no data URI prefix. Returns JSON with fields: ok, path, bytes_written, error.
fs_save_base64_file.name: fs_save_base64_file

data.description: Raw standard base64 content (A-Z a-z 0-9 + / =), ASCII only, with correct padding. Do not include a data URI prefix (e.g. data:image/png;base64,).

path.description: Absolute path where the file will be saved.

fs_search_and_replace.description: Replaces exact text in a file using literal matching. Uses literal string matching (case-sensitive, no regex). Supports dry-run, occurrence selection, optional backup, and optional unified diff output. When occurrence='all', expected_matches is required; if omitted, tool reports match_count and makes no changes. Always returns a JSON string with fields: ok, applied, matched, replaced, path, message, error.
fs_search_and_replace.name: fs_search_and_replace

backup.description: If true and file is modified, creates '<path>.bak' before writing.

diff_context_lines.description: Context lines for unified diff when return_diff=true. Default 3.

dry_run.description: If true, do not modify the file; only report whether replacement would happen.

encoding.description: Optional text encoding. Omit for UTF-8 (default; also UTF-16 with BOM). Otherwise: utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be (also windows-1251, iso-8859-1). Successful edits are written back in the same encoding.

expected_file_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest from file_info(include_hash=true). Edit aborts with stale_file if file content changed.

expected_matches.description: Required when occurrence='all' (if omitted, tool reports match_count and makes no changes). Otherwise optional: if provided, tool fails unless the total number of matches in the file equals this value.

max_diff_chars.description: Maximum number of characters returned in diff output. Default 12000.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence to replace: 'first' (default), 'last', 'all', or 1-based integer index. When 'all', you must also pass expected_matches equal to the total match count.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to modify. Must be a valid file path; directories are not allowed.

replace.description: The new content to replace the found content with. May be multiline. Can be empty to remove the matched content.

return_diff.description: If true, include a unified diff in the result.

search.description: The exact content to find and replace. Match is case-sensitive and literal (not regex). May be multiline. Cannot be empty. Use a unique multi-line snippet to avoid accidental matches elsewhere in the file.

fs_view_image.description: View an image file (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP, BMP, TIFF). Call it when a note in the history points to an image file, to inspect an image in the project, or to look at a screenshot an MCP tool returned: pass the path from the image block of that tool result ("type": "image", "path": ...), not a path mentioned in its text. An image attached to a message (not a note) is already in front of you — answer from it, do not call this tool for it. If you can see images, the image arrives in the next message; otherwise you get a text description of it. Use question to say what to look for.
fs_view_image.name: fs_view_image

path.description: Path of the image file.

question.description: What to look for in the image.

fs_write_file.description: Create or overwrite a text file (optional parent dirs). Keep each call small — stub or first section only. For long documents: minimal write here, then chain append calls with moderate chunks. Huge single `content` often breaks tool-call JSON. Prefer this when you need a new file or full replace; use append to grow an existing file. Pass encoding= to write non-UTF-8 (e.g. cp1251).
fs_write_file.name: fs_write_file

backup.description: If true and file exists, creates a backup copy at '<path>.bak' before writing. Default false.

content.description: Text to write; must be short. For large output: use a placeholder or opening section only, then add the bulk via several append-to-file calls. For code/config, keep to one small file or split across an initial write and appends.

encoding.description: Text encoding to write: utf-8, utf-8-sig, cp1251, koi8-r, latin-1, utf-16, utf-16-le, utf-16-be (also windows-1251, iso-8859-1). Default utf-8.

make_dirs.description: If true, creates any missing parent folders before writing. Set true when the target file's parent folder does not exist yet. Default false — the write fails with 'parent_not_found' if the parent folder is missing.

mode.description: Write mode: 'overwrite' (default), 'create_only' (fail if exists), or 'fail_if_missing' (fail if missing).

path.description: The absolute path of the file to write to. Must be an absolute path, not relative. Ensure the file location is valid and accessible.

project_memory.description: Project/long memory: durable facts for FUTURE sessions ('remember this rule', conventions, artifact-first preferences, stable decisions). Not for turn-by-turn chat progress — use thread memory. Survives restarts. Actions: read, append (short delta), write (full replace / full overwrite; rare). Reports fill percent. Append verified bullets only; no secrets, chain-of-thought, or guesses as facts.
project_memory.name: project_memory

action.description: read = return the current memory content; append = add ONLY the new delta at end; write = fully replace the memory (full overwrite; rare).

content.description: Markdown text for append/write. Required for every action; ignored for read. For append: ONLY the new delta. For write: the FULL updated markdown (full overwrite). For read: pass empty string "".

session_memory.description: Thread/session memory for THIS dialogue only — not project-wide 'remember forever'. Do not append on every trivial step; update after meaningful progress or before handoff/delegation. This tool does NOT write files to disk. Stores compact state that survives dialog summarization. Use fixed registers only: goal = user intent, desired outcome, success criteria, definition of done; constraints = hard requirements, preferences, prohibitions, format/technical/safety limits; state = blockers, active hypotheses, findings in progress, decisions still open — narrative working state. The step-by-step plan with statuses belongs in the session_todo checklist tool when it is available; if that tool is NOT available, keep the plan here instead. Never keep the same steps in both places; knowledge = stable verified facts, architecture decisions, implementation notes, artifact references, evidence. Actions: list, read, append (short delta), write (full replace of one register; rare). Every response includes per-register length vs limit in registers. Use append for compact new deltas only. Use write for full replace: compaction, cleanup, deduplication, or removing obsolete information. Maintenance: when register sizes in that metadata approach or exceed limits, proactively compact the affected register—read it, then write the compact full replacement (deduplicate, drop obsolete detail; do not keep appending into an overfull register). Move bulky details to a file/artifact when needed; keep a concise form of what belongs in that register per the definitions above (e.g. facts, decisions, blockers, artifact links—not chain-of-thought or raw dumps). Do not wait for the user to ask; memory hygiene is part of using this tool. Do NOT store chain-of-thought, verbose reasoning, raw logs, large blobs, full file contents, repetitive history, or transient chatter. Register selection: objective/done criteria -> goal; requirements/preferences -> constraints; blocker/hypothesis/open decision -> state; stable fact/decision/artifact/evidence -> knowledge; step-by-step plan and step statuses -> session_todo tool when available, otherwise -> state. If unsure: an actionable STEP of the task -> session_todo (or state if that tool is absent); other unresolved information -> state; stable reusable information -> knowledge; requirement/preference -> constraints; desired outcome -> goal. Keep memory compact, structured, and durable.
session_memory.name: session_memory

action.description: list = show register sizes; read = return one register; append = add ONLY the new delta; write = fully replace one register (rare; full overwrite).

content.description: Markdown text for append/write. For append: ONLY the new delta. For write: the FULL updated register content (full overwrite).

reason.description: Optional brief justification for why this update is useful and why it belongs in this register. Recommended but optional; content is required for append/write.

register.description: Target memory register. Required for every action (ignored for list).

session_read_stored_tool_output.description: Read a paginated fragment of a previously stored large tool output by output_ref. Pagination uses **characters** (Unicode code points): `offset` + `limit`. Response pages include truncated, total_chars, next_offset, returned_chars. EOF: when truncated=false, next_offset equals total_chars (end of body).
session_read_stored_tool_output.name: session_read_stored_tool_output

limit.description: Max characters to return from offset (not lines or records). Clamped to tool_output_inline_max_chars.

offset.description: Character offset (Unicode code points) into the stored body. Default: 0.

session_think.description: Think out loud during the current turn. Use it when complex reasoning, self-critique, or structured reflection is needed. Content is NOT saved to thread memory or any other durable storage—it only exists in the current dialogue context. If your think output contains a specific Decision / Canonical target / Plan completed / Verified fact, record it separately via the thread memory tool (append) when one is available so it can persist across summarization.
session_think.name: session_think

critics.description: Self-critique: what could be wrong, weak points, alternative views.

doubts.description: Uncertainties, open questions, or things that need verification.

reflection.description: Synthesis or meta-reflection: main takeaways, conclusions, next steps.

thoughts.description: Reasoning, hypotheses, or exploration of ideas.

session_todo.description: Task checklist for the CURRENT task — your plan and progress tracker. USE IT PROACTIVELY, without being asked: write the checklist BEFORE starting work whenever the task has 3+ logical steps, several deliverables, or a list of requirements to satisfy. Planning on paper first is how you avoid dropping requirements halfway through — do not rely on memory for multi-step work. Then keep it current as you go: mark a step completed right after finishing it and set the next one to in_progress (exactly one in_progress at a time); add steps when new work surfaces. Each call FULLY REPLACES the checklist with the list you pass; replace the whole list when the task itself changes, pass an empty list to clear it. Skip the checklist only for genuinely trivial or single-step tasks. It survives dialog summarization and is shown to the user as live progress.
session_todo.name: session_todo

todos.description: Full replacement checklist: every remaining and completed step of the current task, in execution order.

content.description: Step formulation (imperative, concise).

skills_list.description: List available local skills. By default returns flat skills plus one entry per pack (the pack's bootstrap skill, marked with 'is_pack_bootstrap': true and 'pack_size': N). Internal pack skills are hidden by default. Use the 'pack' parameter to drill into a specific pack's internal skills. Each list entry has fields: id (canonical, '<pack-id>:<skill-id>' for pack skills), name, description, source (system/user/project), pack_id (string for pack skills, null for flat), is_pack_bootstrap (bool). Bootstrap entries also have 'pack_size' (total internal skills count). Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, error, result}.
skills_list.name: skills_list

pack.description: Pack ID to drill into internal skills only (including bootstrap). When unset, returns flat skills plus one bootstrap entry per pack.

skills_load.description: Load a specific skill by its id — the FIRST step for any skill, before skills_read_reference or skills_read_asset. Returns metadata, instructions, and lists of available references and assets (load those by name afterwards if needed). Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, skill_id, error, result}. On success, result.skill contains the skill detail.
skills_load.name: skills_load

skill_id.description: The id of the skill to load.

skills_read_asset.description: Load ONE supplementary asset file of a skill by slug. This does NOT load the skill itself — call skills_load(skill_id) FIRST to get the skill's instructions and the exact asset names. Use only slug values listed by skills_load (or returned in this tool's error); never invent a slug. Assets live under the skill's assets/ directory. Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, skill_id, slug, error, result}. On success, the asset content is inside result.
skills_read_asset.name: skills_read_asset

skill_id.description: The id of the skill whose asset you want to load.

slug.description: Slug of the asset. Maps to a file path inside assets/, without extension, with '/' as path separator.

skills_read_reference.description: Load ONE supplementary reference file of a skill by slug. This does NOT load the skill itself — call skills_load(skill_id) FIRST to get the skill's instructions and the exact reference names. Use only slug values listed by skills_load (or returned in this tool's error); never invent a slug. References live under the skill's references/ directory. Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, skill_id, slug, error, result}. On success, the reference content is inside result.
skills_read_reference.name: skills_read_reference

skill_id.description: The id of the skill whose reference you want to load.

slug.description: Slug of the reference. Maps to a file path inside references/, without extension, with '/' as path separator.

skills_run_script.description: Run a Python script that belongs to a specific skill. script_name is required and must be one of the skill's listed scripts. Use argv for CLI positional arguments and flags (for example, '--input report.pdf'). args is a legacy JSON object string, supplied to stdin only when argv is absent. Returns a JSON string envelope: {tool, ok, script_ok, skill_id, script_name, argv, args, error, result}. ok=true means the wrapper launched the script; script_ok=false when result.exit_code != 0. On success, the script output is inside result.
skills_run_script.name: skills_run_script

args.description: Must decode to a JSON object (dictionary), not an array, scalar, or null. When provided, pass script arguments as one JSON string (this field is string-typed, not a nested object). The script receives the parsed object on stdin and must read it explicitly (keys are not converted to CLI flags or positionals). Example: '{"input":"hello","limit":3}'.

argv.description: CLI arguments passed after the script path, as entered in a terminal. Example: '--input report.pdf --format json'. When set, args is ignored.

script_name.description: Required script file name inside the skill's scripts/ directory. Use an exact name returned by skills_load; the scripts/ prefix is accepted.

skill_id.description: The id of the skill whose script should be executed.

turn_ask_human.description: Finalizes turn: no. Request user input and wait for their reply. Use to ask for a choice, clarification, missing data, or explicit confirmation before risky or irreversible actions. Do NOT use for one-way status or explanations. Do NOT use as the final report of a completed task or to end the current user turn. Be clear and include necessary context; avoid vague questions. The `question` must be concise: the actual question plus minimal context only. Do not put long comparisons or background dumps into `question`; put detailed material in a separate artifact and reference it briefly here. When a finite choice set fits, prefer explicit options (A/B/C, numbered list, yes/no). After each call, follow the hint field in the tool result to classify and act on the reply.
turn_ask_human.name: turn_ask_human

question.description: Concise question to the human (markdown ok): what you need from them, minimal context, and explicit options when choices are known. Not for long content — use an artifact + short pointer here.

turn_finish.description: Finalizes turn: yes. Call exactly once when you end the current user turn (not the whole thread/session). Use for done / partial / blocked outcomes with a self-contained report and machine-readable handoff. Do NOT use for brainstorming, mid-task status, or progress while work continues. Call only after reasonable work and verification for this turn when needed. Do not call early just to return control.
turn_finish.name: turn_finish

comment.description: Caveats, risks, unresolved items, or suggested next steps for the user.

handoff.description: Must decode to a JSON object (dictionary), not an array, scalar, or null. Pass the object as one JSON string (this field is string-typed, not a nested object). Machine-readable payload for downstream workflows; use "{}" when nothing extra is needed. Example: '{"artifacts":["report.md"]}'.

solution_type.description: Turn outcome: full_solution (objective done), partial_solution (meaningful progress, not done), direct_answer (direct answer/explanation completed this turn), couldnt_solve, need_additional_info (blocked), abandoned.

task.description: What the user asked this turn, in 1–2 phrases, in the user's terms. Not what was done — that is task_report.

task_report.description: Final human-facing summary for this turn: what was done, result, assumptions, evidence. Plain text, no markdown. Max 10000 characters. Not for mid-task status updates.

turn_intermediate_reply.description: Finalizes turn: no. Intermediate user-visible reply: status, hypothesis, mini-explanation, or progress update. The current task is NOT complete — you will continue with more tools after this. Do NOT use for the final report of a multi-step task or to end the current user turn. Do NOT use when you need the user's answer — this tool does not wait for a reply. Keep `answer` concise; for long material use a separate artifact and put only summary + path in `answer`. Omit `artifact_path` when there is no artifact; if the tool schema requires every key (strict mode), pass "" instead. When set, path must be non-empty.
turn_intermediate_reply.name: turn_intermediate_reply

answer.description: Concise intermediate user-facing text (status, partial insight, short clarification). Not a final task report. For long content: short summary here; full text in artifact.

artifact_path.description: Path to a detailed user-facing artifact when long content lives in a file.

turn_propose_plan.description: Finalizes turn: yes. Available ONLY in the 'plan' permission mode. Propose the finished implementation plan to the user for approval and end the turn. Call after research is complete; the user will approve, request rework, or cancel. Do NOT use for progress updates or questions (use turn_ask_human for questions). When a plan is already proposed and the user has not reviewed it yet, never replace it silently. A new request on the SAME task: propose an updated plan in full — the earlier steps plus the new ones, so nothing the user has not seen is lost. A request on SOMETHING ELSE: first ask via turn_ask_human whether to do the pending plan first, replace it, or merge both tasks into one plan, and propose only after they answer. When the user asks to SEE the current plan again or to approve it, do not retell it and do not claim it is approved: call this tool with show_current=true (and an empty plan) — the stored plan is shown again unchanged and the user gets the choice.
turn_propose_plan.name: turn_propose_plan

plan.description: The complete plan in markdown: goal, ordered steps, files to touch, verification. Self-contained — the user approves exactly this text.

show_current.description: true — show the plan already stored in the session again, unchanged (pass an empty plan). Use when the user asks to see or approve the current plan. Not for a plan under rework: propose the updated plan in full instead.
